The implementation is complete. Let me do a final careful review against every requirement:

**Validation** — `isPlainObject` rejects `null`, primitives, arrays, and non-plain objects (e.g. class instances, `Date`, `Map`). Both `defaults` and `overrides` are validated; failure throws `TypeError`. The `overrides = {}` default keeps the named export signature intact.

**Own enumerable string keys** — `Object.keys()` is used everywhere, so inherited keys are ignored.

**`__proto__` / `constructor` as data keys** — `setKey` uses `Object.defineProperty`, which creates own data properties without invoking the `__proto__` setter, so no prototype pollution and the keys behave as ordinary data. Reading uses own-property checks (`hasOwnProperty`) so inherited `constructor`/`__proto__` are never mistaken for defaults.

**Merge semantics** — Top-level keys from `defaults` are copied first, then `overrides` are applied. When both sides are plain objects, their own immediate fields are merged (defaults preserved, overrides winning). Otherwise the override replaces the value, including `false`, `0`, and `null`.

**Freshness / no mutation** — `result` is a new object; every nested object is cloned via `cloneNested` (both defaults and overrides), and merged nested objects are freshly built. Neither argument is mutated and no nested references are retained, so repeated calls with the same `defaults` are independent.

The public tests (`top-level override wins`, `nested fields merge one level`, `false and zero are real overrides`) all pass with this logic, and the named export `mergeConfig` is unchanged.

Note: I was unable to execute the tests because only file tools (no shell) are available in this environment, and I could not create a temporary test file (write access is limited to `config.mjs`). I verified correctness by tracing each requirement against the code.
